short: Understanding the Outstanding High-Voltage Performance of NC
title: Understanding the Outstanding High-Voltage Performance of NCM523||Graphite Lithium Ion Cells after Elimination of Ethylene Carbonate Solvent from Conventional Electrolyte

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: High-voltage 4.5 V NCM523||graphite cells are needed, but the state-of-the-art EC-based electrolyte fails by rollover fading. Eliminating EC from the conventional LiPF6 carbonate electrolyte should keep the cell working and remove the high-voltage failure.
states.detail: Absorbed: n1 (HYP/need), n2 (HYP/hypothesis), n3 (DES/variable_sweep), n4 (PRC/synthesis), n5 (PRC/stimulus), n15 (DES/modification), n16 (PRC/stimulus). Premises: LiDFP (LiPO2F2) is a degraded LiPF6 species, formed in situ during ageing, that decomposes to LixPOyFz including PO3F2-

states.title: Structure state
states.head: On the EC-based graphite anode, transition-metal deposits and Li dendrites sit at the same localized spots; the EC-free anode has no such spots. Far more transition metal is present on the graphite anode after 100 cycles with the EC-based than with the EC-free electrolyte.

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: Negative crosstalk: TM dissolves at the cathode, deposits on graphite and seeds Li dendrites that consume active Li and short the cell. The EC-based cell fails by penetration of Li dendrites that create micro short-circuits.
states.detail: Absorbed: n9 (MEC/pathway), n10 (PRP/behavior_class), n11 (PRP/value), n13 (PRP/value), n14 (MEC/pathway), n18 (MEC/identification). Premises: Rollover fading is known to result from electrode crosstalk: TM dissolution at the cathode and deposition on the anode; A sudden random rise in specific charge capacity and voltage noise indicate penetrating Li dendrites and micro short-circuits; EC is highly reductive; without it LiPF6 is preferentially reduced at graphite to LixPFy species

states.title: Performance state
states.head: EC-based cells collapse by rollover fading from about cycle 45, while EC-free cells keep ~160 mAh/g over 100 cycles at 4.5 V. 1 wt% LiDFP suppresses rollover fading in the EC-based electrolyte and has no significant effect on the EC-free one

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: Removing EC suppresses rollover fading at 4.5 V because in-situ generated LixPOyFz scavenge TMs and stop the detrimental crosstalk

nodes.title: evidence, F8
nodes.head: High-F LixPOyFz rises from ~0.5 to ~8.5 at% on the anode and from ~3 to ~10 at% on the cathode for the EC-free electrolyte, while anode carbonates fall from ~11 to ~4.5 at%. Total degraded LiPF6 on the anode is nearly the same for the two electrolytes (~10 vs ~11.5 at%); only its high-F LixPOyFz part grows
nodes.solves: Surface layers of the EC-free cells hold ~8-10 at% high-F LixPOyFz on both electrodes
nodes.note: stack boundaries read off the 0-100 at% axis; LiF also rises on the anode (47 to 59 at%) and falls on the cathode (65 to 53 at%) the text says the portion of degraded LiPF6 products is significantly higher for EC-free; on the anode bars the sum of the three P2p bands changes little and the change is a redistribution from low-F to high-F LixPOyFz
nodes.detail: o13: High-F LixPOyFz rises from ~0.5 to ~8.5 at% on the anode and from ~3 to ~10 at% on the cathode for the EC-free electrolyte, while anode carbonates fall from ~11 to ~4.5 at%; a3: Total degraded LiPF6 on the anode is nearly the same for the two electrolytes (~10 vs ~11.5 at%); only its high-F LixPOyFz part grows
nodes.inner_audit: a3: the text says the portion of degraded LiPF6 products is significantly higher for EC-free; on the anode bars the sum of the three P2p bands changes little and the change is a redistribution from low-F to high-F LixPOyFz

nodes.title: evidence, F5
nodes.head: From cycle ~67 the EC-based charge capacity jumps randomly to 200-400 mAh/g while its discharge capacity sinks to ~130; the EC-free cell holds ~170 for both. The 85th-cycle charge curve of the EC-based cell carries voltage noise on a 4.5 V plateau running to ~385 mAh/g; the EC-free curve is smooth and ends at ~165
nodes.solves: The EC-based cell fails by penetration of Li dendrites that create micro short-circuits
nodes.note: the scattered charge points run from cycle 67 to 88 and stop; after cycle 90 only the decaying discharge branch remains the arrow labelled 'Voltage noise' marks ripples of well under 0.1 V between ~170 and ~300 mAh/g; the feature is small but visible
nodes.detail: o10: From cycle ~67 the EC-based charge capacity jumps randomly to 200-400 mAh/g while its discharge capacity sinks to ~130; the EC-free cell holds ~170 for both; o11: The 85th-cycle charge curve of the EC-based cell carries voltage noise on a 4.5 V plateau running to ~385 mAh/g; the EC-free curve is smooth and ends at ~165
nodes.necessity_reason: Only figure-backed support with image_support shown for n10 (o10, o11).

nodes.title: evidence, F8
nodes.head: Adding PO3F2- decolourises the violet Co2+ and yellow Ni2+ electrolytes, with 761 to 1 ppm Co2+ and 730 to 5 ppm Ni2+
nodes.solves: LixPOyFz species (PO3F2-) scavenge dissolved TM ions, cutting Co2+ and Ni2+ from ~761 and ~730 ppm to ~1 and ~5 ppm
nodes.note: the colour loss is unmistakable for Co2+ and slight for Ni2+; the Mn2+ result (651 to 1 ppm) is in the linked text only, not in the panel
nodes.detail: o15: Adding PO3F2- decolourises the violet Co2+ and yellow Ni2+ electrolytes, with 761 to 1 ppm Co2+ and 730 to 5 ppm Ni2+
nodes.necessity_reason: Only figure-backed support with image_support shown for n13 (o15).

nodes.title: evidence, F2, F3
nodes.head: First-cycle charge capacity is ~232 mAh/g for the EC-free cell against ~225 for the EC-based one, and its discharge branch ends ~13 mAh/g higher. At cycle 5 the two voltage profiles coincide: ~180 mAh/g charge capacity and the same hysteresis.
nodes.op: compare across conditions, match to reference, read characteristic point
nodes.note: the panel is annotated 'Cycle 1 (19 mA g-1)' while the caption says 0.1C = 79 mA g-1; the caption's 'slight plateau at ~3.3 V' appears in the image as a small shoulder near 3.45-3.5 V, hence partial the grey EC-based trace is completely hidden under the blue EC-free one, so coincidence is shown but the EC-based curve cannot be inspected separately
nodes.detail: o3: First-cycle charge capacity is ~232 mAh/g for the EC-free cell against ~225 for the EC-based one, and its discharge branch ends ~13 mAh/g higher; o4: At cycle 5 the two voltage profiles coincide: ~180 mAh/g charge capacity and the same hysteresis; o6: With Al2O3-NCM523 the EC-based decay starts only at cycle ~65 and reaches ~125 mAh/g at cycle 100; the EC-free cell holds ~170
nodes.necessity_reason: n6 keeps shown support from o5, a2 after removal.

nodes.title: evidence, F3
nodes.head: The EC-based capacity falls abruptly from ~170 mAh/g at cycle ~45 to ~60 at cycle 85, while the EC-free capacity fades smoothly to ~158 at cycle 100. After cycle ~85 the EC-based capacity partly recovers (60 to 82 mAh/g) and the error bars span about +/-40 mAh/g
nodes.solves: EC-based cells collapse by rollover fading from about cycle 45, while EC-free cells keep ~160 mAh/g over 100 cycles at 4.5 V
nodes.note: the text describes the rollover as a sudden severe decay and never mentions the recovery or the cell-to-cell spread
nodes.detail: o5: The EC-based capacity falls abruptly from ~170 mAh/g at cycle ~45 to ~60 at cycle 85, while the EC-free capacity fades smoothly to ~158 at cycle 100; a2: After cycle ~85 the EC-based capacity partly recovers (60 to 82 mAh/g) and the error bars span about +/-40 mAh/g
nodes.inner_audit: a2: the text describes the rollover as a sudden severe decay and never mentions the recovery or the cell-to-cell spread

nodes.title: evidence, F9
nodes.head: With 1 wt% LiDFP the EC-based cell fades smoothly to ~168 mAh/g over 100 cycles instead of collapsing to ~60. In the EC-free electrolyte the curves with and without LiDFP overlap and both end at ~158 mAh/g after 100 cycles
nodes.solves: 1 wt% LiDFP suppresses rollover fading in the EC-based electrolyte and has no significant effect on the EC-free one
nodes.note: the LiDFP-free trace and its error bars are the same data as F3a
nodes.detail: o16: With 1 wt% LiDFP the EC-based cell fades smoothly to ~168 mAh/g over 100 cycles instead of collapsing to ~60; o17: In the EC-free electrolyte the curves with and without LiDFP overlap and both end at ~158 mAh/g after 100 cycles

nodes.title: evidence, F1
nodes.head: Ionic conductivity of both electrolytes rises with temperature; the EC-free curve lies below the EC-based one (4 vs 7 mS/cm at 20 C) and they meet at -40 C. The two overcharge curves superimpose: the same LNMO plateau at 4.7 V and the same decomposition plateau at 5.5 V
nodes.op: compare across conditions, match to reference
nodes.note: read off the axes: at 20 C EMC ~4.0 and EC:EMC ~7.0 mS/cm; both ~1 mS/cm at -40 C; error bars only on the EC-based points the EC-free (blue) trace deviates visibly only between 150 and 200 mAh/g, where it rises to the 5.5 V plateau slightly earlier
